record.what_it_does: Lightspeed-owned hosted ecommerce platform that embeds online stores in any site.
record.auth_notes: Public apps use the OAuth2 authorization-code flow. The token exchange is POST https://my.ecwid.com/api/oauth/token with client_id, client_secret, code, redirect_uri and grant_type=authorization_code. The GET variant was discontinued in March 2025. REST calls send the token as an HTTP bearer header; the OpenAPI scheme is bearerFormat secret_token. Passing tokens in query params was discontinued in March 2025. Tokens are per app per store and do not expire. Each store has a secret_token for server use and a public_token that is safe for the storefront. Custom (private) apps let a store owner get tokens from Ecwid admin > Custom apps without the OAuth flow.
record.access_notes: Only stores on paid plans can use the API. Ecwid no longer lists a free plan: Starter costs $5/month, Venture $35, Business $65 and Unlimited $149. Developers can email Ecwid for a free paid-plan upgrade on a test store, so building is effectively free but needs that support step. Listing a public App Market app needs a submission review (typically 1-2 business days), approval for every update, and a signed partner contract with revenue share. The pricing page lists "Access to App Market" under Venture, so merchants on Starter may not be able to install public apps (unverified).
record.api_breadth_notes: REST API v3 at https://app.ecwid.com/api/v3/{storeId}. It covers store profile, products (about 50 endpoint pages), categories, orders (about 26), customers, discount coupons, shipping and payment options, Instant Site (about 30), dictionaries and more. The docs' llms.txt lists roughly 200 endpoint-level pages; that is an estimate, not an exact count.
record.mcp_notes: I found no official Ecwid or Lightspeed MCP server for the store API. The GitBook docs site has a docs-search MCP endpoint at docs.ecwid.com/~gitbook/mcp, but it only searches documentation and is not an API server. Third-party MCP servers exist from Zapier (zapier.com/mcp/ecwid), viaSocket, Truto, Jentic, Unified.to and Mushrooms.
record.blocker_notes: A toolkit acting for many merchants needs a public OAuth app. That means App Market review (1-2 business days, with every update re-approved) and a partner contract with revenue share. Development works on a test store after emailing support for a free paid-plan upgrade. Only paid-plan merchants can use the API.
